rationale:
runtimes/csharp/Telemetry.cs: The schema change renames speed_mps to speed_kph with unit change from m/s to km/h. Producer must scale input by 3.6 before serialization. Consumer observes speed_kph in output JSON. Speeding threshold updates from 30 m/s (108 km/h) to 108 km/h directly using the converted value. All three candidates require modifications to align with the new field name, unit, and threshold.
runtimes/python/telemetry_runtime.py: Schema change renames speed_mps to speed_kph and changes unit from mps to kph. Request provides speed in mps, so producers must scale by 3.6 before serialization. Threshold for speeding becomes >108.0 kph. Observation key becomes speed_kph. Wire field 2 remains float32. Entity v1/v2 unchanged per spec.
runtimes/typescript/telemetry.ts: Schema rename from speed_mps to speed_kph with unit conversion at encoding time (mps * 3.6 = kph). Threshold for speeding changes from 30.0 mps to 108.0 kph (same physical speed). Observation key changes from speed_mps to speed_kph. The TypeScript bindings generate speedKph for the protobuf field speed_kph. All three candidates are required references that must be edited to maintain correct behavior through the full request->encode->decode->observe path.
assumptions: runtimes/csharp/Telemetry.cs: The regenerated protobuf bindings expose SpeedKph property for field 2
runtimes/csharp/Telemetry.cs: Entity.SpeedKph is populated correctly when parsing base64 payload
runtimes/csharp/Telemetry.cs: JSON output uses double-precision JSON numbers for float32 values
runtimes/csharp/Telemetry.cs: No mixed version/unit scenarios to handle
runtimes/python/telemetry_runtime.py: Protobuf float32 values serialize as-is; Python float multiplication produces double but protobuf encodes as 32-bit
runtimes/python/telemetry_runtime.py: The generated VehicleTelemetry class now has speed_kph field instead of speed_mps
runtimes/python/telemetry_runtime.py: The threshold 108.0 corresponds to 30 mps * 3.6 = 108 kph
runtimes/typescript/telemetry.ts: TypeScript protobuf bindings use camelCase speedKph matching protobuf snake_case speed_kph
runtimes/typescript/telemetry.ts: Float32 precision is handled by protobuf library; we expose the decoded value directly
runtimes/typescript/telemetry.ts: Entity fields use the same naming convention as generated bindings (speedKph not speedMps)
runtimes/typescript/telemetry.ts: No mixed unit/version handling needed; coordinated rollout only
